questions.heading: The Header Says What the Solver Received
questions.stem: Your model should have 120 rows: a budget row for each of 20 years and a capacity row for each of 100 sites. The first line of the HiGHS log says `LP plan has 220 rows; 3400 cols; 9120 nonzeros`. What does that tell you?

options.text: Presolve added 100 rows of its own, which happens before any iteration
options.says: The first line describes the model as received, before presolve; and presolve removes rows, it does not add them.

options.text: The log counts nonzeros with the rows, so the two counts do not compare
options.says: The header reports rows, columns and nonzeros separately; 220 is the row count alone.

options.text: Scaling added a row per site, which happens when coefficient ranges are wide
options.says: Scaling multiplies existing rows and columns by factors; it adds no rows.

options.text: The model holds rows you did not mean to add, such as site rows added twice
options.says: Right: the header is the model as built, and 100 extra rows match one capacity row per site added a second time.

questions.heading: A Failed Run's Objective Line Means Nothing
questions.stem: A nightly script stores the number on the `Objective value` line of each HiGHS log. Last night's footer read `Model status : Infeasible` and `Objective value : 0.0000000000e+00`. What should the script have stored?

options.text: No objective at all, as only an optimal run's objective is an answer
options.says: Right: only an Optimal status makes the objective line an answer; HiGHS prints the line on every run.

options.text: An objective of 0, as the footer gives the value of the empty plan
options.says: An infeasible model has no allowed plan, empty or not; the 0 is printed with no plan behind it.

options.text: The last objective among the iteration lines, as that plan was closest
options.says: No point the solver passed on its way to proving infeasibility is an allowed plan, so none has a value to store.

options.text: The objective with its sign flipped, as HiGHS works on a minimization
options.says: The sign flip applies to the iteration lines, not the footer, and it does not turn an infeasible run into an answer.

questions.heading: GLOP and PDLP Logs Carry the Same Facts in Other Words
questions.stem: A row of a PDLP progress table reads: rel_prim_res 2.1e-07, rel_dual_res 4.0e-08, rel_gap -3.5e-03. The run's tolerance is 1e-06. Has the run converged at that row?

options.text: Yes, as a negative gap means the dual objective is already beaten
options.says: The gap can have either sign; it is its size that must be small, and 3.5e-03 is far above 1e-06.

options.text: Yes, as two of the three measures are well below the tolerance
options.says: PDLP stops only when all three measures are within the tolerance.

options.text: No, as the gap is far larger in size than the tolerance
options.says: Right: primal and dual residuals are small, but the primal and dual objectives still disagree by far more than 1e-06.

options.text: No, as the primal residual is still above zero
options.says: PDLP stops within a tolerance; a small nonzero primal residual is normal at the end, as the lesson's last table row shows.
